Galaxy Girls – Visitation School - Plant the Moon Challenge – Summer 2021 
1 
Title: 
How does the addition of water absorbing beads to a mixture of lunar regolith and 
garden soil affect the growth of plants. 
 
Hypothesis : 
We think that a mixture of lunar regolith simulant with water absorbing beads and 
potting soil will be the best mixture for growing a variety of plants. 
 
Independent Variables or Parameters: 
We are changing the mixtures of soils in our pots, as well as the type of plants we are 
growing. Our control container consisted of 100% Miracle Grow Potting soil. 
 
We planted five containers which consisted of a soil mixture of 50% by volume lunar 
regolith simulant and 50% by volume of Miracle Grow potting soil. 
 
We planted five containers which consisted of a soil mixture of 50% by volume lunar 
regolith simulant, 25% by volume of water absorbing beads, and 25% by volume of 
Miracle Grow potting soil. 
 
The plants selected to grow from seeds were spinach, peapod, Dakota blue corn, luffa 
gourd, violet bean, lavender, and cucumber. Corn seeds, luffa gourd seeds, and violet 
bean seeds were planted in the same container for companion planting following the 
traditional Native American planting known as the Three Sisters. This method has the 
beans helping to fix nitrogen to the soil, the corn provides stability for the beans, and 
the big gourd leaves protect the soil. All other seeds were individually planted and not 
companion planted. 
 
While lavender is not an edible plant, it was selected for its calming scent properties, 
as a consideration for the mental health and well-being for a crew during a long 
duration lunar mission. 
 
Dependent Variable: 
We expect that the size and mass of the plants grown from seeds in the soil mixture 
containing water absorbing beads to be larger and have more mass than those not 
grown in this mixture. 
 
Measurements: 
We measured the mass of the plants after the growing period and took final readings 
on how big the leaves were. 
 
Controls: 
All plants and soil mixtures received the same amount of light via a red and blue LED 
plant growth light. Our initial plant set up did not have a grow light, and within several

Galaxy Girls – Visitation School - Plant the Moon Challenge – Summer 2021 
2 
weeks they all became too leggy, broke easily, and were not ok. We replanted after 
the mid-point check-in with the addition of a red and blue grow light. 
 
The larger pots of soil received the same amount of water, 60 mL, and the smaller pots 
received the same amount of water, 30 mL, all plants were watered every other day. 
 
Results: 
We found that the majority plants that were planted in the soil mixture of 50% by 
volume lunar regolith simulant, 25% by volume of water absorbing beads, and 25% by 
volume of Miracle Grow potting soil did the best and were the biggest with the most 
mass. The two exceptions were lavender and spinach, neither seeds grew in either 
environment. We think this is because both of those types of plants require a very 
specific growing environment to get started, and we couldn’t germinate them on the 
paper towels like we have in the past. 
 
We took each plant out of the soil, removed the soil from the roots, and then weighed 
them. We noted that most of the seeds planted in the lunar regolith simulant, soil, and 
water absorbing beads mixture germinated and grew into plants, while not all of the 
seeds planted in the lunar regolith simulant and soil did. 
 
We were surprised by just how big the difference was in the violet bean plants! The 
plants growing in the lunar regolith simulant, soil, and water absorbing beads grew 
about 2 cm bigger at the end than the ones that grew in the lunar regolith simulant 
and soil mixture. 
 
We concluded that the plants that grew in the soil mixture with water absorbing beads 
grew better because the soil was able to keep in more water and slowly feed the plant, 
compared to all of the water that seemed to run through the lunar regolith simulant 
and soil.

Our initial plantings and first sprouts June 10th & June 15th. 
 
 
 
Our peapod plants grew quickly, but soon we learned that the lack of consistent light 
meant that our plants wouldn’t be very strong or hardy. Right before the mid-point 
check-in, July 10th. We tried to save the plants, but it was too late. 
 
 
 
 
Attempt #2: We added a variety of plants and LED grow lights, July 12th.

July 16th Our first plants sprouted and the addition of the grow light really helped!
 
 
One day later, July 17th, the plants are really taking off! 
 
 
July 24th the plants are all doing really well. Except the lavender and spinach still 
haven’t sprouted.

July 31st We noticed that the LED grow lights are helping the plants become really green. 
 
 
 
August 4th The plants in the water absorbing beads soil continue to do really well. 
 
 
August 10th It’s time to find out if our hypothesis was correct!
